title: Canonical base-change map for a right adjoint
statement: Given a cartesian square of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes X'=X\times_Y Y' with g_X:X'\to X, f':X'\to Y', f:X\to Y, and g:Y'\to Y [def-pc-fibre-product], let a and a' be right adjoints to Rf_* and Rf'_* on quasi-coherent derived categories [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-derived-direct-image, lem-pc-qcqs-derived-direct-image-right-adjoint], and let \beta: Lg^*Rf_*\to Rf'_*Lg_X^* be the canonical base-change transformation on D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(X) (the adjoint, under Lg^*\dashv Rg_*, of Rf_*(\eta):Rf_*\to Rf_*Rg_{X,*}Lg_X^*=Rg_*Rf'_*Lg_X^*, with \eta the unit of Lg_X^*\dashv Rg_{X,*} [def-pc-derived-pullback]). Assume \beta is an isomorphism. Let \theta: Rg_{X,*}a'\to aRg_* be the conjugate of \beta, i.e. the transformation between the right adjoints of Rf'_*Lg_X^* and Lg^*Rf_* corresponding to \beta; \theta is an isomorphism because \beta is. For K in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(Y), the canonical right-adjoint base-change morphism Lg_X^*a(K)\to a'(Lg^*K) is the composite $$Lg_X^*a(K)\xrightarrow{Lg_X^*a(\eta'_K)}Lg_X^*aRg_*Lg^*K\xrightarrow{Lg_X^*(\theta_{Lg^*K})^{-1}}Lg_X^*Rg_{X,*}a'(Lg^*K)\xrightarrow{\epsilon}a'(Lg^*K),$$ where \eta':\mathrm{id}\to Rg_*Lg^* is the unit of Lg^*\dashv Rg_* and \epsilon is the counit of Lg_X^*\dashv Rg_{X,*} [def-pc-derived-pullback] (Stacks, duality.tex, equation-base-change-map).

source.place: Tag 0AA8 (Lemma 48.6.2), equation-base-change-map and definition preceding case (1)

proof.text: The fibre product node supplies X'=X\times_Y Y' and its projections g_X and f'; the displayed commutative square is therefore cartesian. The quasi-compact and quasi-separated hypotheses allow the derived categories and derived direct images in the statement to be formed.

By [lem-pc-qcqs-derived-direct-image-right-adjoint], Rf_* and Rf'_* preserve D_{\mathrm{QCoh}} and the restricted functors have right adjoints a and a'; its hypothesis holds because f, f', g, g_X are morphisms between quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphisms. By [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-adjoint], Lg^*\dashv Rg_* and Lg_X^*\dashv Rg_{X,*} on D(\mathcal O), with units and counits used below. These adjunctions restrict to the full subcategories D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}: Rg_* and Rg_{X,*} preserve D_{\mathrm{QCoh}} by [lem-pc-qcqs-derived-direct-image-right-adjoint], and Lg^*, Lg_X^* preserve D_{\mathrm{QCoh}} by [lem-pc-derived-pullback-tensor-qcoh]. Composing adjunctions, Lg^*Rf_*\dashv aRg_* and Rf'_*Lg_X^*\dashv Rg_{X,*}a' as functors D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(X)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(Y').

source.place: Tag 0AA8, definition of the base-change map and adjunctions

proof.text: The unit \eta of Lg_X^*\dashv Rg_{X,*} gives Rf_*(\eta):Rf_*\to Rf_*Rg_{X,*}Lg_X^*. Since f\circ g_X=g\circ f' (the square commutes), [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-composition] gives Rf_*Rg_{X,*}\cong R(f\circ g_X)_*=R(g\circ f')_*\cong Rg_*Rf'_*, so the adjunction Lg^*\dashv Rg_* transposes this map to the canonical natural transformation \beta:Lg^*Rf_*\to Rf'_*Lg_X^*.

The conjugate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] of \beta:Lg^*Rf_*\to Rf'_*Lg_X^* with respect to the two composite adjunctions of Step 2 is a transformation \theta:Rg_{X,*}a'\to aRg_*. The conjugate bijection preserves isomorphisms, so the hypothesis that \beta is an isomorphism implies that \theta is an isomorphism and \theta^{-1} is defined.

For K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(Y), the unit \eta'_K:K\to Rg_*Lg^*K, the component (\theta_{Lg^*K})^{-1}:aRg_*Lg^*K\to Rg_{X,*}a'(Lg^*K) and the counit \epsilon:Lg_X^*Rg_{X,*}\to\mathrm{id} exist by Steps 2 and 4. Applying Lg_X^*a to the first and Lg_X^* to the second, then composing with \epsilon at a'(Lg^*K), gives exactly the displayed composite Lg_X^*a(K)\to a'(Lg^*K), which is therefore well defined.
